Freehold Telok Ayer Street conservation shophouse hits the market at $23.76 mil
article:
A freehold conservation shophouse at 171 Telok Ayer Street in Chinatown has been launched for sale through an expression of interest (EOI) exercise. The three-storey property with a mezzanine has an indicative price of $23.76 million, or about $5,700 psf on its estimated total floor area of 4,168 sq ft.

The shophouse occupies a 1,390 sq ft commercial plot in the Telok Ayer Conservation Area in District 1. It is currently fully occupied, with an F&B operator on the ground floor and office occupiers on the upper floors, according to CBRE, which is handling the sale.

The property has regular and efficient floor plates that can accommodate a wide variety of businesses. The upper floors could potentially be converted to alternative uses such as restaurants, wellness facilities or serviced apartments, subject to approval from the relevant authorities, CBRE adds.

Telok Ayer Street is a large thoroughfare stretching from Market Street in Raffles Place to Anson Road in Tanjong Pagar. In Chinatown, shophouses line the road, largely tenanted by a mix of eateries, retail shops and offices.

Clemence Lee, CBRE’s executive director of capital markets for Singapore, noted that freehold and 999-year conservation shophouses in Districts 1 and 2, including properties along Circular Road , Keong Saik Road and Stanley Street, have transacted at prices between $16 million and $22 million, or between $5.000 and $6,800 psf, over the last six months.

“Given the 171 Telok Ayer Street’s palatable investment quantum of under $25 million, we expect it to draw strong interest from a wide pool of investors, including corporate investors, family offices and high-net-worth individuals,” he added.

The property is within walking distance of four MRT stations: Telok Ayer (Downtown Line), Tanjong Pagar (East-West Line), Shenton Way and Maxwell (Thomson-East Coast Line).

The EOI exercise will close at 3pm on Nov 25.

title: Johor landed homes: What's attracting Singaporean buyers and what they should know
article:
Johor's landed housing market has recorded substantial growth over the past decade, supported by the Malaysian state's expanding economy, rising investments and improving connectivity with Singapore.

These factors and trends are adding to interest in Johor's residential property market, including among Singaporeans considering landed homes across the Causeway for retirement or as a second residence.

The opportunities in Johor's property market and what Singaporean buyers should know before making a purchase were explored at a two-day event in Singapore organised by JLand Group (JLG) and EdgeProp Singapore on Oct 17 and 18.

The event featured presentations by Ng Ming Yang, property research analyst at EdgeProp Singapore ; Vincent Kek, sales manager, JLG; Chan Fei Loong, senior partner, Lim Soh & Goonting Advocates & Solicitors; and Ryan Khoo, co-founder and director, Alpha Marketing.

They covered topics including Johor Bahru's economic and property market outlook, the appeal of landed homes to Singaporean buyers, JLG's Sanubari development at Bandar Dato' Onn, and the legal requirements and considerations for foreign purchasers.

The discussions also explored how retirement plans, the Malaysian ringgit and the upcoming Johor Bahru–Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link could influence interest in the market.

Audience members also took the opportunity to engage the speakers in lively question-and-answer exchanges during each session.

Strong economic growth, deepening integration with Singapore

Johor's residential market has benefited from the state's economic expansion, with the state’s real gross domestic product growth outpacing Malaysia's national average in recent years.

In his analysis of the property market, Ng from EdgeProp Singapore highlighted Johor’s economic performance and the stronger price growth recorded by landed homes compared with high-rise properties.

The state’s economy grew 8% in 2025, outpacing the nationwide 5.2%, according to data from the Department of Statistics Malaysia.

Johor also attracted the highest investments across all states last year — surpassing the likes of Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Penang — and made up 26% of the country’s total approved investments.

Of this, foreign direct investment accounted for a large share for Johor, totalling RM60.52 billion ($18.97 billion), compared to RM35.06 billion or less for the other three.

"It shows that international companies have confidence in Johor," said Ng.

"Global tech firms such as Nvidia, Microsoft and ByteDance are choosing to set up data centres there, and the state is also attracting investments in other high-tech industries such as manufacturing and semiconductors."

Moreover, Johor and Singapore are set to become more integrated amid bilateral commitments, namely the upcoming Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link, and the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone.

Connectivity in particular will be a catalyst, with the RTS Link expected to open in February 2027, improving travel between Johor Bahru and Singapore.

"The RTS offers more certainty in terms of travel time," Ng said. "That's quite crucial because you can start going beyond the Johor Bahru city centre and go somewhere less dense, with more peace and quiet."

Terraced homes outperform high-rise properties

Meanwhile, Johor's landed housing market has performed more strongly than its non-landed or high-rise residential segment.

Prices of terraced houses in the state have grown by 7.2% annually from 2016 to 2025, increasing every year including during the Covid-19 pandemic.

In contrast, prices of high-rise homes have lagged, rising by 1.9% annually over the past decade. They only recovered to pre-pandemic levels in 2025.

Within Johor, its capital city Johor Bahru and Kulai exhibited the highest terraced property price growth during the last 10 years, at compound annual growth rates (CAGR) of 9.3% and 8% respectively.

The supply picture also differs: terraced houses in Johor face far less incoming supply than high-rise units, relative to existing stock.

In Johor Bahru, the number of unsold, completed terraced houses has been declining steadily over the past five years, shrinking from 1,150 in 2021 to 307 in 2025.

“The supply of terraced homes in Johor is tight, and there’s quite a healthy absorption,” Ng noted.

Freehold landed homes in an established township

For prospective buyers in Singapore, the appeal of Johor's landed housing market often depends on the location, surrounding amenities and type of homes available.

At the event, Kek from JLG introduced Sanubari, a freehold landed residential development within the group's established 1,474-acre (597ha) Bandar Dato' Onn township in Johor Bahru.

The 762-unit project's latest release, Phase 4A , comprises 105 double-storey terraced houses, each with four bedrooms and four bathrooms and spanning built-up areas of 2,160 sq ft.

They offer space for larger households, including families and those considering a second home in Johor.

Prices range from about RM1.3 million to RM1.95 million.

The freehold properties carry individual titles, as opposed to strata titles, and sit on either corner or intermediate lots measuring 20 feet by 70 feet (6.1m by 21.3m).

Kek noted that the first three phases of the project are fully sold, with the launch of the final Phase 4B, comprising 117 units, targeted for the end of this year.

Sanubari “blends nature, technology, community and personal space”, which fosters wellbeing and purpose, he added.

Buyers are attracted to the project’s community-focused design, active lifestyle facilities, smart home automation system, as well as ample green spaces and landscaped areas.

The homes are equipped with rooftop solar panels, can be fitted with EV charger points and come with parking for two to three cars. Residents can enjoy an exclusive clubhouse, pool and central park.

In the vicinity are Aeon Mall and Fairview International School, with healthcare accessible at the KPJ Bandar Dato’ Onn Specialist Hospital, highlighted Kek.

Unlike newer projects in relatively undeveloped locations, Sanubari in Bandar Dato' Onn is nestled within a “very mature” suburban area of Johor Bahru, he added.

It sits near other established residential and commercial townships including Taman Mount Austin, Taman Daya, Taman Setia Indah and Bandar Jaya Putra.

Bandar Dato’ Onn has 5,827 existing and committed residential units thus far, and is well-connected with convenient access to the surrounding neighbourhoods and the North-South Expressway.

JLG’s plans for Bandar Dato' Onn go further than Sanubari. The township will also include the upcoming Calmore Estate and Calmore Hills developments, which are projected to bring onstream 6,101 units.

What Singaporeans should know before buying

Johor's landed homes may appeal to Singaporeans considering a second residence or looking to retire across the Causeway.

However, prospective buyers need to be aware of the restrictions and requirements governing foreign property ownership in Malaysia, including those specific to Johor.

Chan of Malaysian law firm Lim Soh & Goonting outlined the key legal and procedural considerations for Singaporean buyers.

These included stamp duty, real property gain tax, eligible property types, inheritance, key contractual terms when purchasing residential properties, reselling in the future, Bumiputera release lots, and ownership restrictions.

One of the key rules in Johor is the state’s minimum purchase threshold of RM1 million for foreign buyers, Chan highlighted.

Among landed residential properties in Johor, Singaporeans can purchase terraced, cluster, semi-detached and detached houses that are two storeys or higher, as well as vacant bungalow lots, though foreign ownership quotas and state consent requirements apply.

Chan also delved into the sale and purchase agreement as well as the respective obligations of developers and purchasers for new-launch units.

As for the Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) initiative, he explained that it is not mandatory before buying any property in the country, though a property purchase is required when applying for the programme. MM2H is a long-term residency initiative by the Malaysian government for foreigners.

For buyers unfamiliar with the property market in Johor and Malaysia, these requirements are important to understand before entering into a transaction.

Retirees, ringgit and RTS

Lifestyle preferences and retirement aspirations are also influencing Singaporeans’ keen interest in Johor Bahru, with the city’s proximity to Singapore and lower living costs among the factors fuelling demand for homes across the Causeway.

Khoo of Alpha Marketing focused on three key drivers of Johor Bahru's real estate market: retirement, the Malaysian ringgit and the upcoming RTS Link.

Retirement in Johor Bahru is attractive to Singaporeans for a few reasons, including the numerous cultural similarities. "Many things in Malaysia are familiar because we have similar foods and languages," Khoo noted.

He reckoned Singapore's ageing population will likely contribute to demand and more residents would want to retire across the border, where living expenses are generally relatively lower given the strength of the Singapore dollar.

Johor Bahru's access to retiree-friendly leisure activities and services is also a strength.

"Malaysia is a big country with a large hinterland and forests. If you stay there, you can very easily reach places like Sabah, Malacca and Kuala Lumpur," Khoo said.

The geographical proximity is another reason Johor Bahru appeals, and improved connectivity with the upcoming RTS Link is set to make cross-border living even more feasible.

For Singaporeans retiring or spending part of their time in Johor Bahru, the short distance allows them to travel between the two cities frequently without the need for air travel.

They can maintain their social and family ties in Singapore while enjoying the lifestyle across the Causeway.

Khoo gave an example of grandparents who could be spending most of their retirement in Johor Bahru while making regular trips back to Singapore to visit their children and grandchildren.

"You can go to Johor Bahru in the morning to have your dim sum and walk around, and return to Singapore by night to play mahjong with your friends. The next day, you may head to Johor Bahru again for a dental appointment and then come back to Singapore to see your children."

He described this as "effectively living in two cities" and having the best of both worlds.

That said, he also encouraged prospective buyers to assess their requirements, intended use of a property and their reasons for wanting to purchase it.

They ought to consider questions such as: Will you drive in Malaysia? How will you manage the property? Who will live with you? How will you enjoy your home and the neighbourhood? When will you need to exit?

Whether buying a home to live in or as an investment, Singaporeans will need to weigh the potential benefits of owning property in Johor against the responsibilities and practicalities involved.

title: GH15 Ventures wins Pek Chuan Building tender with $80.68 mil bid
article:
[Correction: This article has been updated for accuracy and to clarify that GH15 Investments is not a subsidiary of Aw & Sons Capital.]

GH15 Ventures has won the collective sale tender for Pek Chuan Building at 116 Lavender Street with an $80.68 million bid.

Company records show that GH15 Ventures is an investment vehicle of GH15 Investments, a company registered to operate hostels and dormitories for students, workers and others. Its director is Stephen Goh.

The deal was brokered by Terry Wong, head of capital markets and investment sales at Colliers Singapore, who represented the buyer GH15 Investments.

The public tender closed on Oct 7 and drew three bids, says Dillon Loi of Mount Everest Properties, the marketing agent. The winning bid is 4.8% above the $77 million asking price set when the building was relaunched for sale in September. It also tops the $80 million guide price for its first two attempts at a collective sale in October 2025 and March 2026. Both tenders closed without a successful bid.

The site has 28,700 sq ft of land and is zoned commercial, with a plot ratio of 2.5 and a height limit of 12 storeys. At the permissible gross floor area of 71,750 sq ft, the price works out to $1,124 psf per plot ratio (ppr), excluding any land betterment charge and lease top-up premium. The site is on a 99-year lease that started in 1978, leaving about 51 years.

The existing four-storey building has retail space on the first three floors and offices on the fourth. It is about 50m from Bendemeer MRT Station on the Downtown Line and within walking distance of Lavender MRT Station on the East-West Line. Loi describes it as the longest standalone commercial building with a full frontage along Lavender Street.

The buyer can apply to URA for a change of use to a hotel or mixed-use development. If it opts for asset enhancement instead, Loi expects the building to attract offices and F&B businesses displaced by the 2027 redevelopment of Marina Square and Valley Point. He also expects “strong support” from upcoming residential developments in Kallang and Boon Keng.

Refurbishment has paid off for a similar building. Mount Everest Properties sold GSM Building on Middle Road to Coliwoo for $80 million in 2023. After a major refurbishment, the building, now called Coliwoo Midtown , is being acquired by CapitaLand Ascott Trust for $134 million under a deal announced in August.

title: Get Smart: How to Spot a Scam
article:
My jaw dropped.
I couldn’t believe what I was reading.
Surely, he can’t be serious.
Let me set the scene.
Over a decade ago, I had a colleague who was my regular lunch buddy at my previous job.
Given my interest in stocks, the discussion invariably drifted towards
investing
.
My colleague knew what he wanted.
Again and again, he stressed the importance of capital protection, while accepting that it comes with lower returns.
He was adamant on this point.
No problem with that, of course.
So long as you know what you want and know what to expect, you are on the right track.
Then came the surprise.
Out of the blue, he started messaging me about binary options from a dodgy-looking platform.
For the uninitiated, binary options are all-or-nothing bets on whether a price will end above or below a set level at a set time. Get it right, and you collect a fixed payout. Get it wrong, and you lose your entire stake.
The contrast between his capital protection stance and binary options was jarring.
It was befuddling.
How did this conservative investor, who had repeated the same adamant message for 18 months, suddenly decide to try a risky all-or-nothing approach?
So, I told him: Don’t walk away. Instead, RUN away.
Thankfully, he listened.
Sure enough, within months, the dodgy platform was exposed as a scam.
The fall of the rational mind
What bugged me the most was how a rational colleague, who knew what he wanted and knew what to expect, could fall for such a scheme.
Some of us may think that only fools fall for a scam.
But here we have a rational person, who is well educated and well grounded, succumbing to fraud.
What happened?
From what I observe, it’s the promise of huge returns that often breaks the rational mind.
Here’s the thing: my colleague did not stop being rational overnight.
His goals had not changed.
What changed was the number dangled in front of him.
When you have made peace with modest returns, the promise of huge gains can make your sensible plan feel painfully slow.
And once that number takes hold, it starts doing the thinking for you.
The questions you would normally ask — who runs this platform, and where do the returns come from? — quietly fall away.
None of us are immune.
What’s possible, and what’s not
That’s why the recent Nanning scam brought this lunchtime story flooding back.
In early September, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said 52 Singaporeans had been arrested and detained in Guangxi, China, over suspected pyramid scheme activities.
Reports have linked the case to a scheme that asks for an entry fee of 69,800 yuan, or around S$13,000.
The promise?
A payout of up to 10.4 million yuan — almost S$2 million — if you manage to recruit others.
That’s about 150 times your money.
This promise alone should set alarm bells off.
Now, compare that with what’s possible.
Warren Buffett,
arguably the greatest investor of our time, compounded
Berkshire Hathaway
‘s (NYSE: BRK.B) share price at 19.7% a year from 1965 to 2025.
Over the same 61 years, the
S&P 500
(INDEXSP: .INX) returned 10.5% a year, including
dividends
.
Even at Buffett’s pace, turning S$13,000 into almost S$2 million would take around 28 years.
At the S&P 500’s pace, you’d need about 50 years.
So, when someone promises 150 times your money, ask yourself: is this person better than Buffett?
If the answer is no, the money has to come from somewhere else.
In a pyramid scheme, that somewhere else is the next person who signs up.
That’s the hallmark of fraud.
Get Smart: Let your goals be your alarm
So, how do you spot a scam?
Start with what my colleague got right in the first place.
He knew what he wanted. He knew what to expect.
That is your best defence.
When an offer promises returns that are wildly out of line with what you expect, don’t treat it as an opportunity.
Treat it as an alarm bell.
And when an offer asks you to abandon the very goals you have held on to for so long, that’s your cue to do what I told my colleague.
Don’t walk away.
RUN.

title: STI Downturn: 3 Temasek-Linked S-REITs to Watch
article:
When the market falls, unit prices grab all the headlines.
The distributions underneath them rarely do.
At the close on 14 October 2026, the
Straits Times Index
(SGX: ^STI) sat 7% below its 52-week high.
Before you rush to press the sell button, it is worth checking whether the underlying income stream behind each unit is still growing.
Temasek, a global investment company headquartered in Singapore, holds a deemed interest in the three
Singapore real estate investment trusts
(S-REITs) below.
Let’s look at how these three REITs are actually performing under the hood.
REIT
Temasek’s deemed interest
As at
CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust (SGX: C38U)
21.4%
27 February 2026
CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (SGX: A17U)
18.6%

Mapletree Logistics Trust (SGX: M44U)

Is CICT’s DPU growth keeping pace with its larger unit base?
CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust (CICT) is Singapore’s largest REIT by market capitalisation.
It owns retail, office and integrated development properties, with total assets of S$28.2 billion as at 30 June 2026.
For the first half of 2026 (1H2026), CICT’s gross revenue rose 7.5% year on year (YoY) to S$846.8 million.
Net property income (NPI) grew 8.7% to S$630.5 million, while distribution per unit (DPU) climbed 7.1% to S$0.0602.
Here’s the thing: CICT’s unit base grew 5.8% over the period.
DPU still grew faster.
In simple terms, every existing unit earned a bigger piece of the pie.
Stepping up to full ownership of CapitaSpring and bringing in income from Gallileo in Frankfurt drove most of this growth, helping offset the sale of Bukit Panjang Plaza.
Portfolio occupancy rose 0.4 percentage points quarter on quarter to 95.6%, while rental reversions came in at 4.0% for retail and 6.5% for office.
CICT completed its S$3.9 billion purchase of Paragon on 1 July 2026, shortly after the half closed.
Management expects to wrap up selling Asia Square Tower 2 for roughly S$2.45 billion in the second half of the year.
Until that transaction officially closes, it remains an execution risk worth monitoring.
Aggregate leverage sat at a healthy 37.4%, and average cost of debt held steady at 2.9%.
Related articles:
Keppel DC REIT vs CICT: Which REIT Would I Buy Today?
Unlocking CICT’s Growth Engine: From AEIs to a S$1.1B Hougang Expansion
Why did CLAR’s DPU barely move when income grew 8.6%?
CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (CLAR) owns 234 properties across Singapore, Australia, the US, the UK/Europe and Japan, with a portfolio valued at S$20.1 billion as at 30 June 2026.
In 1H2026, CLAR’s gross revenue rose 6.7% YoY to S$805.5 million.
NPI rose 6.2% to S$556.1 million, and distributable income climbed 8.6% to S$359.4 million.
DPU, though, rose just 0.1% to S$0.07482.
So where did the growth go?
CLAR raised equity in both 1H2025 and 1H2026.
It now spreads a bigger income pool across more units.
The underlying business grew, but unit dilution kept the payout per unit virtually flat.
Rental reversion reached 8.5%, and management expects high single-digit reversions for the full year.
CLAR completed S$1.1 billion in acquisitions during the half and plans to divest Kim Chuan Telecommunications Complex for S$200.4 million, reflecting a 32% premium to its valuation.
On the flip side, occupancy fell to 89.1% from 91.8% a year ago.
Two newly completed properties dragged the figure down.
Without them, occupancy would have been 90.3%.
Aggregate leverage stood at 39.7%, and cost of debt at 3.5%.
Related articles:
CICT vs CapitaLand Ascendas REIT: Which CapitaLand Giant Is the Better Buy?
Singapore REITs Report Earnings: What Investors Should Know About CLAR, CLAS, MPACT and MIT
Can MLT grow its DPU through currency and China headwinds?
Mapletree Logistics Trust (MLT) owns 175 logistics properties across nine Asia-Pacific markets, with assets under management of S$13.1 billion as at 30 June 2026.
Keep in mind that MLT’s financial year ends in March, so its latest set of figures covers 1QFY2027 and does not line up directly with the half-year figures above.
Gross revenue rose 0.8% YoY to S$178.9 million, NPI grew 2.0% to S$156.4 million, and DPU edged up 0.2% to S$0.01816.
A new warehouse in Mumbai and a full quarter from Mapletree Joo Koon Logistics Hub added revenue.
Weaker China contributions, divested assets and softer Asian currencies pulled the other way.
Excluding
currency effects
, gross revenue and NPI would have grown 2.0% and 3.1% respectively.
Borrowing costs fell 2.7% YoY to S$38.3 million.
After the quarter, MLT announced the sale of three properties worth about S$155 million, including 39 Changi South Avenue 2, which is being sold at a 20.3% premium to valuation.
The risks sit in the operating numbers.
Occupancy slipped to 96.4% from 96.9% three months earlier.
Rental reversion was 0.9%, or 2.3% excluding China.
At 40.5%, MLT’s aggregate leverage is the highest of the three.
Related articles:
The Logistics Boom: Why Mapletree Logistics Trust Is a Global Powerhouse
CLI, MLT, FLCT and PLife REIT Earnings: What Investors Should Know Now
Get Smart: Watch the payout, not just the price
When the index falls, ask yourself one question before taking action: Is the cash distribution shrinking, or is it just the unit price?
Put
DPU growth
side by side with distributable income growth.
If the two move together, the REIT is passing its growth on to you.
If income races ahead of DPU, check the unit count.
CLAR shows how fundraising can mask a growing business when you look only at DPU.
Will this year’s acquisitions add more income per unit than the new units cost?
DPU will tell you, one reporting season at a time.

title: Musk seizes on SpaceX momentum with push towards Tesla merger
article:
(Oct 21): Elon Musk capitalised on a strong quarter of earnings at SpaceX to openly press for combining the business with Tesla Inc in what would be the biggest merger of all time.

Towards the end of a call about SpaceX results that far exceeded expectations, the chief executive officer initially said he was “tap dancing through a minefield” when asked about the prospect of merging the two companies currently worth a total of almost US$3.5 trillion ($4.5 trillion).

“I have to be thoughtful about what I say here,” Musk said.

The world’s richest man then let loose with inside-the-boardroom details, disclosing for the first time that both SpaceX and Tesla had formed special committees to consider the idea. The committees consist of independent directors, Musk said, and he can’t be part of the discussions because he’s a conflicted party.

That didn’t stop Musk from offering his view.

“Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes,” Musk said. After cautioning that getting enough support from Tesla shareholders may be tricky and that neither committee has settled on terms, he reiterated his support not once, but twice.

See also: Foxconn buys US$727 mil stake in Mitsubishi Electric unit making EV parts

“There’s a lot of merit to combining the companies,” Musk said. “I think it would be a good idea, but it’s really up to the special committees of both companies.”

SpaceX and Tesla shares both extended gains following the comments, climbing as much as 8.6% and 1.7%, respectively, in late trading. SpaceX is the larger of the two, having closed with a market capitalisation of US$2 trillion.

A merger of SpaceX and Tesla would be a blockbuster, creating a conglomerate spanning electric vehicles, energy storage batteries, rockets and satellites. The stated rationale for bringing those disparate interests together lies in their shared ambitions to leverage artificial intelligence for data centres in space, driverless cars and humanoid robots.

See also: UniCredit gets ECB go-ahead to take control of Commerzbank

“There’s no question that Musk wants the merger, and he wants to get it done sooner rather than later,” said Gene Munster, the founder of Deepwater Asset Management, which has invested in both companies. “It was a key question on the call, and Elon said it was a good idea about three times. He’s getting people excited about it, and he wants to bump up the enthusiasm.”

Musk made the comments after SpaceX posted US$4.4 billion in net income for the quarter ended in September, far better than analysts’ average projection of US$1.88 billion. Revenue increased 161% from a year ago and also beat expectations.

Revenue from SpaceX’s AI business — now going by super intelligence, or SI — soared to US$7.56 billion in the quarter, more than nine times what the company generated a year ago. SpaceX has become a major compute and infrastructure supplier to Anthropic PBC, Alphabet Inc and others, and in August acquired Cursor, the developer of a popular AI-powered coding tool.

Those factors — along with increased adoption of Grok, the large language models developed by Musk’s xAI — contributed to SpaceX’s AI business posting US$431 million of income from operations in the third quarter. A year ago, the business recorded a US$1.7 billion loss.

“Super Intelligence was the standout growth driver for the quarter,” SpaceX chief financial officer Bret Johnsen said during the call, pointing to increased demand from clients seeking more computing power, as well as Grok enterprise sales.

SpaceX expects total revenue to rise to as much as US$37 billion in the first quarter of next year, Johnsen said. He indicated that the company expects to keep borrowing, saying there are “a number of available pools of debt capital that we are talking to at the moment”.

SpaceX said subscribers to its satellite-internet service Starlink — its biggest income generator — reached 13.6 million by the third quarter, short of the number analysts were expecting. Revenue from the company’s connectivity business still managed to beat expectations, rising 69% from a year ago to US$5.25 billion.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Whereas SpaceX’s AI and connectivity businesses have taken off, revenue from the company’s unit focused on designing, manufacturing and operating launch vehicles and spacecraft rose just 6% to US$1.77 billion in the third quarter.

On a conference call, Musk said SpaceX expects to catch both the booster and the ship for the 15th test flight of his giant Starship, planned for next month. The vehicle is expected to be fully reusable, a feat no other rocket has achieved. President Gwynne Shotwell later added that the company expects to attempt the first demonstration of on-orbit refuelling with Starship early next year.

On-orbit refueling will be necessary for Starship to master for SpaceX’s contract to land humans on the moon for Nasa. The company is supposed to have a prototype ready by next year that can dock with Nasa’s Orion spacecraft for Artemis III mission, a precursor to a moon landing planned for 2028. Whether that will be ready on time remains uncertain.

Starship is also essential for launching upgraded Starlink satellites that can provide greater capacity and data speeds than the current spacecraft in orbit. Shotwell said she expects the additional capacity from flying what the company refers to as V3 Starship satellites on a much larger vehicle will allow SpaceX to expand across new markets.

“Connecting cars, robots and the adoption of super intelligence will increase communication demands not in percentages, but in many orders of magnitudes,” Shotwell said. “We expect Starlink alone to represent a significant portion of global internet traffic.”

Starlink’s growth was driven by momentum in the aviation industry for in-flight Wi-Fi and Starshield, a militarised version of the service that is more encrypted and secure, Johnsen said.

Starshield has come under renewed scrutiny since Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused the White House and Musk of placing restrictions on the technology, which his country’s forces have used for battlefield communications and operations. Both Musk and Trump have denied involvement in the limitations, igniting a firestorm over technology that’s become indispensable to Ukraine’s war against Russia.

When commenting on a potential SpaceX-Tesla combination, Musk said that he suspects “people out there assume” the merger is a certainty. While he said this would be an overstatement, the deal would have the support of Chad Anderson, the chief executive officer of Space Capital, an early SpaceX investor.

“It makes a ton of sense,” Anderson said. “Combined, it would be the only company owning the full physical-AI stack, from chip fabrication to orbital data centres to autonomous devices on the ground. No competitor has an analogue.”

title: Anthropic may spend US$750 bil in coming years, report says
article:
(Oct 21): Anthropic PBC could spend US$750 billion ($959 billion) on additional computing power in the coming years, according to a Wall Street Journal (WSJ) report, as the company prepares for an initial public offering (IPO).

The AI firm had a net loss of US$80.7 billion in the first half of 2026, the media outlet reported, citing a draft IPO prospectus. That compares to a net loss of US$13 billion in the corresponding period a year ago, the WSJ said.

The overwhelming majority of the net loss in the first half of this year, US$72 billion, resulted from accounting charges linked to changes in the value of convertible notes and other instruments Anthropic has issued, according to the report.

Anthropic, one of the leading artificial intelligence (AI) developers, is expected to publicly file paperwork for a Wall Street debut in the coming weeks, setting it up for what could be one of the largest IPOs ever. The listing will help the company raise additional capital to support its investments in chips, data centres and talent to build new and better AI models.

The company behind Claude spent close to US$9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure in the six months ended June 30, versus US$2.3 billion in the same period in 2025, according to the WSJ. Anthropic deployed more funds to secure computing power in the first half of 2026 than in all of 2025, when it spent US$7.3 billion.

The prospectus showed Anthropic’s extensive web of computing power agreements — totalling around US$450 billion in the next seven to 10 years — the majority of which can’t be cancelled, according to the WSJ. The company plans to spend US$111 billion on contracts with Alphabet Inc’s Google Cloud, US$110 billion with Amazon.com Inc’s Amazon Web Services and US$31 billion with Microsoft Corp.

See also: AI fears return with data centre firm Elice’s 33% debut flop in Seoul

Anthropic’s prospectus flags the risk of damages caused by AI, including the potential for models to show “self-preserving” qualities to avoid being turned off, and responses that resemble “blackmail” to keep humans from preventing them from operating, the report showed. Anthropic could also face the risk of political resistance to building data centres in the US, where most of its capacity is, according to the WSJ.

The company told investors it had achieved profitability in the third quarter on an adjusted basis, Bloomberg News has reported. Anthropic is generating positive free cash flow, had a gross margin of 85% and an over 11% positive adjusted operating margin as of the third quarter, people familiar with the matter have said.

The company is set to begin formally marketing its IPO as soon as the week of Nov 9, putting it in line to begin trading before the US Thanksgiving holiday, Bloomberg News has reported. It is expected to make its debut no later than the end of the year.

title: US-Mexico trade talks hit impasse as Lutnick exerts influence — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 21): US and Mexican trade negotiators have hit an impasse over tariffs on steel and aluminum, dashing earlier optimism for an imminent deal and likely kicking major progress until after the midterm elections, people familiar with the matter said.

Talks have cooled off in recent days after US officials including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick took issue with Mexican officials’ demands for reduced tariffs on metals, according to two of the people, who asked not to be identified discussing private deliberations.

Lutnick has sought to exert more influence in the talks and broader trade policy after taking a back seat to US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, whose office earlier spearheaded the negotiations, according to the people. Lutnick met virtually with Mexico’s President Claudia Sheinbaum on Sept 9.

The White House and Commerce Departments did not respond to requests for comment.

Mexican officials had earlier expressed hope that a deal was within the negotiators’ grasp. One sticking point is around lowering tariffs on derivative metals products. Duties on downstream products made from steel and aluminum have amassed to cover a substantial part of Mexico’s economy, and Mexican leaders have said they did not want a deal without relief on that.

Talks between the two countries stalled after a counter-proposal from Lutnick failed to address Mexican concerns, the people said. Now, US officials have grown comfortable with the idea of kicking a potential deal down the road, well after the Nov 3 midterm elections.

See also: Brazil moves to contain bird virus, suspends chicken exports to Malaysia

“We’re a little bit stuck on the details,” Roberto Lazzeri, Mexico’s ambassador to the US and one of several officials who have participated in US trade negotiations, said Monday on a panel in Miami. The Wall Street Journal first reported the impasse in talks.

“I think the sticking point is the 232 tariffs,” Lazzeri said, referring to the duties imposed by the Trump administration under Section 232 of the Trade Act of 1974, which include a 50% import tax on steel and aluminum, and a 25% import tax on for non-US content on USMCA-compliant cars.

Mexico’s Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard, who is Mexico’s lead negotiator, rejected the suggestion that Lutnick was blocking a potential deal.

See also: Japan’s export growth stays solid, supported by chips, cars

“In my last conversation with him, I didn’t get the impression that he was opposed to reducing those tariffs, at least as far as I know,” Ebrard told reporters late last week.

A framework agreement between the US and Mexico would provide stability and certainty to business leaders who are stalling investment decisions amid rolling negotiations over renewing the US-Mexico-Canada trade deal. Another point of contention has been industry-specific tariff rates, which Mexican officials have argued give other countries, including Japan and Korea, an upper hand.

Mexico’s economy is heavily dependent on trade with the US, with more than 80% of its exports going to its northern neighboru. The government has sought a deal that would see US tariffs on light vehicles go to 15% from the current 25%, according to other officials, who also asked not to be identified. The proposed agreement also included a reduction in the 50% tariffs on steel and aluminum, although the two sides had not settled on a new rate.

The disagreements echo those that caused the breakdown of US and Canada talks in August, which was largely driven by Lutnick’s opposition to proposed concessions on industry specific, Section 232 tariffs — which fall under the Commerce Department’s jurisdiction.

On Tuesday, Sheinbaum struck a positive note about reaching “the best possible” trade deal.

“We haven’t reached a final agreement yet, but we’ve come quite a long way,” she said at a daily press briefing.

title: DayOne said to weigh options for US IPO after data centre rout
article:
(Oct 21): DayOne Data Centers Ltd is weighing options for its US initial public offering (IPO), including a potential delay or size cut, as volatility around data centres increases, according to people familiar with the matter.

While Singapore-based DayOne has been waiting for the right window to launch the IPO, it has also been considering the possibility of pushing back the share sale until the market recovers, the people said. Other options include going ahead with a smaller listing that may raise US$2.5 billion ($3.2 billion) to US$3 billion, roughly half of what it had originally aimed for, the people said.

DayOne, whose backers include Coatue and Hillhouse, is continuing to engage with potential investors and still wants to move forward as soon as the market allows, the people said. The company was initially considering raising as much as US$5 billion from the listing as soon as the fourth quarter, people familiar with the matter said previously. It had been eyeing a valuation of about US$20 billion, the people have said.

Deliberations are ongoing and DayOne hasn’t made any final decisions, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private. The company could still opt to move ahead with the offering in the coming weeks, according to the people. DayOne declined to comment.

While data centres have drawn global investor demand amid a boom in sectors related to artificial intelligence (AI), a more negative sentiment has started to have ripple effects on IPOs. DayOne has been raising billions of dollars in private funding rounds as it seeks capital to build out its pipeline.

Australian data centre company Firmus Grid Ltd pulled its roughly US$5 billion IPO when investors balked at the valuation it sought, while AirTrunk, which also operates data centres, delayed a planned real estate investment trust IPO in Singapore to next year.

See also: GCash owner erases gains in debut after record Philippines IPO

South Korean digital infrastructure company Elice Inc plunged 32% in its Seoul trading debut on Tuesday. Coreweave Inc’s shares have more than halved since their May peak, and Nscale Ltd is facing pushback over its target IPO valuation, Bloomberg News has reported. On Wednesday, shares of Australian data centre operator Nextdc Ltd plummeted after it cut earnings guidance.

Some investors are hoping that the recent market volatility will pass after the US midterm elections on Nov 3. They are also looking ahead to the performance of Anthropic PBC’s upcoming listing as an important gauge of sentiment towards the AI sector.

DayOne filed for a US IPO earlier this month. The offering is being led by Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan Chase & Co, Bank of America Corp and Citigroup Inc. IFR reported on Monday that DayOne was gathering more investor feedback before launching the share sale.

See also: Singapore's Sea starts enterprise cloud foray while eyeing fintech arm IPO

DayOne is running or developing data centres in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Hong Kong, Japan, Finland and Spain. Other backers include GDS Holdings Ltd, the SoftBank Vision Fund and Citadel’s Ken Griffin.

title: Brazil moves to contain bird virus, suspends chicken exports to Malaysia
article:
SAO PAULO (Oct 21): Brazil raced to contain the trade fallout from the detection of a highly contagious bird virus, as poultry shipments to countries including top buyer China faced restrictions.

Brazil said Monday that Newcastle disease was identified at a commercial turkey unit in the state of Santa Catarina. The discovery prompted a restriction in trade with several partners, raising the risk of disruptions from the world’s largest poultry exporter that is also home to meatpacking giants including JBS NV and MBRF Global Foods SA.

So far, however, the impact has been fairly limited. Brazil briefly suspended all poultry shipments to China before negotiations resulted in restrictions covering only Santa Catarina. In other major markets including Saudi Arabia, South Korea and the UK, even narrower limits were imposed, around the affected area.

In a previous outbreak of the disease in 2024, Brazil had to halt shipments to China and the European Union. On that occasion, it took 18 months before trade with China was fully restored, with authorities clearing shipments from the state where the virus was detected.

“Unless we see a widespread event happening — which is unusual for this disease and Brazil’s Ministry acted fast to contain spread — we think the impact could be even smaller” amid the limited restrictions, JPMorgan analysts led by Lucas Ferreira wrote in a note.

Newcastle disease attacks the respiratory, nervous and digestive systems of birds. While there’s no evidence that the virus could be transmitted to humans by food, it is typical that importing countries set protocols for shipments, partly as a way of protecting their own producers. 

The virus was found in a turkey that did not present any symptoms, according to Brazil’s Animal Protein Association, or ABPA. To prevent the virus spread to the flock, authorities ordered the culling of all 6,000 animals in the affected production facility.

See also: Japan’s export growth stays solid, supported by chips, cars

Santa Catarina is Brazil’s second-largest supplier of chicken, accounting for roughly 23% of all exports this year through September. Meatpacking companies with plants there may seek to use other plants outside the state to continue serving countries that imposed restrictions.

“The market is seeing very strong demand, and exports will grow this year,” said Ricardo Santin, president of ABPA.

In China’s case, an agreement between the two nations required Brazil to “self-embargo,” although authorities from the Asian nation have the ability to lift or ease restrictions, Santin said.

See also: Maersk and Hateco plan US$3.5 bil Vietnam rail freight project

The situation differs from market to market. Brazil halted all poultry shipments to Malaysia, while Mexico also suspended imports of Brazilian poultry. On a more limited basis, Brazil has restricted shipments from Santa Catarina state to Kazakhstan and Chile, in accordance with sanitary agreements with those countries.

Restrictions are even narrower for some other destinations, with bans limited to processing plants located near the area where the virus was detected. Those measures apply to countries including Argentina, South Africa, Saudi Arabia, the UK and South Korea.

title: Japan’s export growth stays solid, supported by chips, cars
article:
(Oct 21): Japan’s export growth remained solid in September, with shipments of chips and cars rising.

The value of exports rose 16.7% from a year earlier, the Finance Ministry reported Wednesday. That missed economists’ median forecast of a 21.3% increase. Exports have risen for 13 straight months.

Imports rose 18.9%, compared with economists’ estimate of a 20.4% advance. The trade balance was an unadjusted ¥536 billion (US$3.4 billion) deficit, compared with a ¥1.1 trillion deficit in August.

The gain in exports highlighted ongoing demand related to artificial intelligence. Shipments of semiconductors and chip-making equipment surged 49.4% and 43.9%, respectively. Car exports gained 15.1%.

By destination, shipments to the US gained 22.9%. Those to China and the European Union advanced 8.6% and 10.5%, respectively.

Imports of crude oil gained 51.1% by value, compared with a 3.1% increase in volume, as oil prices remained elevated due to tensions in the Middle East.

See also: Maersk and Hateco plan US$3.5 bil Vietnam rail freight project

“Demand for AI-related products remains strong, with semiconductor exports rising, and I expect this trend to continue without any oversupply for the foreseeable future,” said Takeshi Minami, chief economist at the Norinchukin Research Institute. “The situation in the Middle East is spiraling out of control, so high oil prices are likely to persist for some time.”

Japan has been reducing its dependence on oil from the region by cultivating alternative sources. Japan’s crude oil imports from the US jumped 820% by value in September, while shipments from the Middle East gained 1.5% by value. In volume terms, oil imports from the region fell 30%.

Japan’s trade surplus with the US was ¥393 billion. The Trump administration has imposed higher tariffs on Japanese goods in an effort to narrow the US trade deficit with Japan. The two nations struck a trade deal last year that capped tariffs at 15% on most Japanese products in exchange for Tokyo’s pledge to increase investment in the US.

See also: US homebuilder sentiment drops to 14-year low on depressed sales

The yen traded at 157.43 against the dollar on average in September, 6.7% weaker than a year earlier, according to the ministry. A weaker yen makes it more expensive to import materials while it gives exporters a competitive advantage overseas.

title: US stock futures advance on AI earnings boost
article:
(Oct 21) : Asian stocks were set to track US stock futures higher as strong earnings from some of the biggest beneficiaries of the artificial intelligence boom helped revive the tech trade.

Futures for the Nasdaq 100 jumped 1% after SpaceX reported quarterly net income that more than doubled estimates, sending its shares up more than 5% in late trading. Contracts for the S&P 500 rose 0.5% after the underlying benchmark advanced 0.3% on Tuesday. Equity-index futures for Australia, Japan and South Korea all pointed to gains.

Super Micro Computer Inc. also topped expectations, lifting AI-infrastructure shares in extended trading. The company has benefited from surging spending on equipment used to train and run AI models. Meanwhile, Netflix Inc. sank after issuing a disappointing forecast.

Elsewhere, Brent crude settled near US$109. Talks aimed at reaching a deal between the US and Iran are continuing, according to a diplomat involved in the negotiations, who pushed back against reports that an agreement was close. Long-term Treasuries outperformed, weighing on the dollar.

The results offered some reassurance after concerns over AI valuations and financing rattled technology shares last week. Investors now turn to a packed earnings slate for signs that growth can justify the billions being poured into computing infrastructure, with Meta Platforms Inc. due to report Wednesday.

“There are no signs that demand for AI is slowing,” said Angelo Kourkafas at Edward Jones. “We’re seeing healthy skepticism and a maturation of the theme, moving away from an environment where everything AI-related goes up toward a greater focus on quality and the companies with the deepest pockets to finance the investment needed to meet demand.”

See also: Oil steadies as traders weigh conflicting signals on Iran talks

Elon Musk’s satellite, rocket and AI conglomerate posted US$4.4 billion in net income for the quarter ended September, compared with analysts’ average estimate of US$1.88 billion. Revenue surged 161% from a year earlier and also beat expectations.

Separately, Musk said SpaceX and Tesla Inc. have formed special committees to explore a potential merger, a preliminary step toward what would rank as the largest corporate tie-up of all time.

Long-term Treasuries advanced Tuesday as oil retreated from recent highs, easing inflation concerns. Yields from 10 to 30 years fell three to four basis points, with the benchmark 10-year rate declining to 5.11%.

See also: Stocks climb in late hours after SpaceX’s earnings

While oil prices have been a dominant driver of Treasury yields for much of this year, bond investors largely ignored them last week amid a selloff in stocks that have benefited from investment in artificial intelligence.

“The AI risk-off trade that bubbled up last week is still top of mind in rates markets and seems to be driving the price action today, although the move lower in oil also helped put some downward pressure on yields,” said Izaac Brook, US rates strategist at RBC Capital Markets.

title: Oil steadies as traders weigh conflicting signals on Iran talks
article:
(Oct 21): Oil steadied after a choppy session on Tuesday that saw traders parse conflicting headlines on efforts to end the US-Iran war.

West Texas Intermediate traded near US$98 a barrel, while Brent closed below US$109 on Tuesday after trading in a range of more than $6. While talks aimed at ending the conflict are continuing, reports that an agreement is close are inaccurate, according to a diplomat involved in negotiations.

An earlier unconfirmed report on Iran war negotiations had knocked oil off five-month highs, with Brent at one point falling as much as 3.3% before paring losses. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump said he has to make a final decision about which way he wants to win, referring to the conflict.

Brent has surged almost 80% this year as widening conflicts in the Middle East and between Russia and Ukraine disrupt energy supplies, with refined products climbing even more sharply. Renewed attacks on tankers and energy infrastructure are keeping geopolitical risk elevated even as Persian Gulf flows recover to near pre-war levels.

“This conflict doesn’t feel like it’s coming to a quick conclusion,” said Dan Pickering, chief investment officer at Pickering Energy Partners. Traders “are settling in for a higher-priced environment while respecting the volatility in the near-end of the curve.”

Separately, the industry-funded American Petroleum Institute reported US crude inventories fell by 4.9 million barrels last week, according to a document seen by Bloomberg. If confirmed by official data on Wednesday, it would mark a third weekly decline.

title: Stocks climb in late hours after SpaceX’s earnings
article:
(Oct 21) : Stocks rose in late hours as SpaceX reported solid earnings fueled by a big jump in its artificial-intelligence business.

An exchange-traded fund tracking the S&P 500 gained after the close of regular trading. Elon Musk’s satellite, rocket and AI conglomerate posted US$4.4 billion in net income for the quarter ended in September, topping the average projection of US$1.88 billion. Super Micro Computer Inc.’s preliminary results beat estimates. Netflix Inc. sank on a disappointing forecast.

In regular hours, more than 400 firms in the US equity benchmark rose. Brent oil settled near US$109. Despite inaccurate reports that a peace agreement between the US and Iran is close, talks aimed at reaching a deal continue, according to a diplomat involved in negotiations. Long-term Treasuries outperformed.

Investors around the world will be closely watching a spate of tech earnings for clues on whether the AI boom can justify the billions of dollars being poured into the industry. Following SpaceX’s results, attention will soon shift to Meta Platforms Inc.’s figures on Wednesday.

The key question is whether recent growth rates can be sustained as comparisons become more demanding and macroeconomic risks persist, according to Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi at UBS Chief Investment Office.

“We expect a strong third-quarter tech earnings season from a fundamental perspective, but elevated expectations may lead to company-specific volatility,” she said.

See also: US stock futures edge higher after chipmaker rally

“AI remains a long-term driver of earnings and economic growth, but investors are becoming more selective about which companies get rewarded from here,” said Anthony Saglimbene at Ameriprise. “For investors, that argues for owning AI exposure selectively rather than broadly, keeping technology concentration in check, and diversifying across market caps, sectors, and regions.”

Marking a sharp reversal from the broad-based rush into AI in recent years, investors are indeed becoming more selective and demanding with their bets on the technology. Elice Inc., a South Korean AI computing supplier scarcely known outside its home market, tanked 32% in its debut in Seoul.

While CoreWeave Inc. shares bounced, they have been under intense volatility as its bonds recently hit distressed levels on concerns over heavy borrowing.

See also: Oil wavers as Iran threats vie with robust Gulf crude flows

“There are no signs that demand for AI is slowing,” said Angelo Kourkafas at Edward Jones. “We’re seeing healthy skepticism and a maturation of the theme, moving away from an environment where everything AI-related goes up toward a greater focus on quality and the companies with the deepest pockets to finance the investment needed to meet demand.”

Kourkafas noted that we’re also seeing earnings growth broaden beyond the largest companies. Against this backdrop, managing exposures is more important than trying to time pullbacks, he said.
